original_question: For a finite-length monomial subscheme type Z = Spec k[x,y]/I on a smooth projective surface S, let Hilb_I S denote the constructible locus in the Hilbert scheme whose closed points are subschemes Y subset S isomorphic to Z. Describe Hilb_I S: is this locus locally closed, and what adjacency relations occur between such loci inside the Hilbert scheme?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Problem 2.4.1 (Regularity for generic monomial zero schemes)
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly fixes a finite-length monomial scheme Z = Spec(k[x,y]/I), places the corresponding isomorphism type inside the Hilbert scheme of a smooth projective surface S, and asks the same two concrete questions as the paper: whether the locus Hilb_I^S is locally closed and what adjacencies occur among such loci.
missing_details: The paper begins with a monomial ideal I subset k[x,y] and sets n = dim_k(k[x,y]/I) < infinity; the relevant ambient Hilbert scheme is Hilb^n(S).
Finite length is unpacked in the paper as: I is (x,y)-primary and Z is supported at the origin.
S is not merely smooth projective; it is an irreducible smooth projective surface defined over the same field k.
The paper states that Hilb_I^S is an irreducible constructible subset of Hilb^n(S), not just an unspecified constructible locus.
The official formulation first asks to describe Hilb_I^S in general, and only then singles out local closedness and adjacency as the main subquestions.
The word adjacency is not formally defined in the paper, so a stand-alone version should spell it out as closure/incidence relations among these loci inside the Hilbert scheme.
Section 2.4 does not impose any extra characteristic restriction here, so the refined question should not add one.
refined_question: Let k be a field, let I subset k[x,y] be a monomial ideal of finite colength n, and set Z = Spec(k[x,y]/I) (equivalently, I is (x,y)-primary and Z is supported at the origin). For every irreducible smooth projective surface S over k, let Hilb_I^S subset Hilb^n(S) denote the irreducible constructible locus whose closed points are the subschemes Y subset S that are isomorphic to Z. Describe Hilb_I^S: in particular, is Hilb_I^S locally closed in Hilb^n(S), and what closure/incidence (adjacency) relations occur among these monomial-type loci inside the Hilbert scheme?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 2.4.1. The surrounding setup in Section 2.4 supplies the hidden data needed to make the question stand alone: I is a monomial ideal in k[x,y], n = dim_k(k[x,y]/I) is finite, this is equivalent to I being (x,y)-primary and Z being supported at the origin, and for each irreducible smooth projective surface S over k there is an irreducible constructible subset Hilb_I^S of Hilb^n(S) whose closed points are the subschemes isomorphic to Z. The next paragraph moves on to Problem 2.4.2 about the cohomology of I_Y tensor O_S(D), so your draft is targeting the geometric problem about the locus Hilb_I^S itself, not the later cohomological conjectures. The later Conjectures 2.4.3 and 2.4.4 are downstream specializations for I = (y, x^r)^m and confirm that Section 2.4 is the right local context, but they are not the statement your draft is trying to capture.
